findings.message: The only daemon-soak machinery on main is `write_report(workspace, stem, report, fs)`, which validates and writes a `DaemonSoakReport` the caller has already built. A repo search shows no bounded soak runner outside tests and seed tests. Nothing runs a daemon for >=24 injected hours on an injected clock, plants the three closed faults (`worker_killed_mid_run`, `conflict_resolution_rungs`, `semantic_conflict_integration_red`), observes each discriminating terminal, records a real `producing_run`, or computes the `auditor` verdict. Under a no-code-change fence, the Implement agent would have to fill in every `observed`/`auditor`/`green` value itself. That is exactly the self-attestation the second acceptance criterion and the Definition of rejected forbid.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: The acceptance criteria need the report to be 'produced by the daemon-soak machinery', while Scope in/out forbid any code change. The merged machinery has no entry point that produces an entry, so the criteria can't all be met under this fence. The plan's clarification also fixes soak-run as 'changes no code', so re-authoring within the caps can't close the gap.
